text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGING - contbatch path p99 SLO breached in us-west-2 - streaming stalls & tail spikes. Dashboard: https://dash.redwood/example/contbatch-p99
maria: ack, saw the alert. I'm oncall. Initial p95/p99 are jumping since 14:03 UTC. p95 ~ 340ms -> 620ms, p99 ~ 720ms -> 2200ms. Streaming stall rate up x8.
ajay: looking... querying queue depths and batch sizes now.
leo: any customer reports yet? could be packing amplification from mixed sequence lengths.
maria: yes two customers reported timeouts (500s) on streaming sessions, support ticket IDs #2345, #2346. Impacted models: open-llama-13b-ish variants on contbatch pool.
ajay: running metrics query: 
```
redwoodctl metrics query --pool=contbatch --since=15m --expr="histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_duration_bucket[5m])) by (le))"
```
Result: p99 spike aligns with increased avg_batch_size (from 18 -> 64) and higher padding ratio. Queue depth for stream-uploads spiked to 320.
leo: that smells like mixed-seqlen amplification where few long requests hold batch windows -> huge batch size and KV cache thrash.
nina: do we have preemption enabled for streaming? if not, streaming gets starved by large batched infer jobs.
maria: preemption currently on, but scheduler fairness seems to be favoring packable batches. I'm seeing packer_latency high. Also KV eviction churn for some model shards.
ajay: quick mitigation options: reduce max_batch_size for contbatch pool, enable stricter stream-priority, or temporarily route streaming to dedicated streaming pool (if capacity exists).
sam: supports preferring lower-latency over throughput for now. Customers need responsiveness.
leo: I can spin up a small dedicated streaming pool in us-west-2 (thin, 2 GPUs) and roll traffic there for affected models. That should reduce tail for streaming.
maria: let's try lowest-risk first: reduce max_batch_size and tighten batch wait window.
```
# commands to run
redwoodctl pool update contbatch --max-batch-size 32 --batch-wait-ms 8
redwoodctl pool update contbatch --stream-priority weighted
```
ajay: applying now. patching config on active nodes.
ops-bot: config-update job started for pool contbatch (job id cj-8801)
ajay: done applying, rolling config. monitoring.
maria: metrics after change (2m): p95 -> 360ms, p99 -> 980ms, streaming stalls down x3. queues down to ~70.
leo: good improvement. still above SLO but trending quickly. I'll proceed to spin up streaming pool as fallback if this doesn't hold.
nina: should we inform affected customers? Ops suggests sending short note "We are mitigating a latency issue; you may see elevated streaming latencies. Working on fix."
sam: +1 notify, include ETA 30m.
maria: I'll update status page and post to #customer-impact.

-- Handoff notes for next oncall (ajay taking):
- current mitigations applied: contbatch max_batch_size=32, batch-wait-ms=8, stream-priority weighted
- monitor p95/p99 for contbatch and streaming stall rate
- if p99 > 1200ms for 10m, spin up streaming-dedicated pool: 
  redwoodctl pool create streaming-fallback --region=us-west-2 --gpus=2 --profile=streaming
  then reroute models: redwoodctl route set model=open-llama-13b --pool=streaming-fallback --percent=30
- if KV churn continues, escalate to eng-runtime with logs + heap profiles (tag: contbatch-kv-churn)

ajay: taking handoff. I'll keep an eye for next 2 hours, set alerts for p99 > 1000ms.
maria: thanks team. setting page escalation to eng-runtime at 15:45 UTC if no improvement. :thumbsup:
ops-bot: reroute job queued (job id cj-8802) if requested.
incident-bot: alert cleared for sustained p99 improvement over 10m. :white_check_mark:
maria: closing thread, followups in #eng-runtime if needed. Thanks everyone.
